correctness.rationale: The proof reduces the exchangeable count law to a binomial mixture with fixed directing mean, computes exact tangent majorants from the maxima of f(p)/p and f(p)/(1-p), verifies central concavity by an explicit quadratic second-derivative certificate, proves least-majorant and greatest-minorant properties, and supplies exact one- or two-atom extremizers. An exact-rational checker independently replays the algebra and finite two-atom stress tests.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Convex order does not determine a single cell probability, and a tail envelope does not algebraically imply a point-mass envelope because extrema of adjacent tails need not be attained by the same directing law. A separate hull calculation is required.

value.rationale: The probability of an exact count is a natural local concentration functional for exchangeable binary data and random-effects binomial models. The theorem gives the full feasible interval, explicit extremizers, and the exact narrow window in which iid sampling is optimal. Outside that window it quantifies a concrete way latent heterogeneity can increase a selected count probability.
